theorem.name: FORCED_CANONICALIZATION_CONFLUENCE_V1
theorem.scope: Let P be one authoritative hard state and F a finite compatible set of authorized forced assignments. Compare only histories that are jointly reachable: every assignment requested by a history is still dynamically forceable when requested, and all histories request exactly F.
theorem.statement: The B2B1 canonical closure depends on the compatible forced assignment set F, not on the order in which the assignments of F are applied. Every nonterminal jointly reachable history ends in the same canonical source state up to canonical relabeling and equivalent independent reconstruction receipts. Every terminal history for F certifies that the batch F-closure is terminal UNSAT as well.

final_seed: The final seed is S_F=S union dom(F), with the same fixed color attached to each forced identity in every history.
Set union of forced identities/assignments is order-independent.
source_masks_and_lists: For every still-present vertex v, the set of colors seen on final seed neighbors is the union of the old seed-color set and the colors contributed by adjacent assignments in F.
This union is independent of order, so final source lists and source-list sizes are independent of order.
singleton_persistence: If a vertex becomes source-singleton Z1 at some prefix, later seed growth can only remove additional available source colors.
Therefore the vertex either remains the same singleton or becomes Z0.
A jointly reachable nonterminal continuation cannot pass through Z0; hence every early promoted singleton is also a singleton of the same color under the final seed.
Conversely any final Z1 vertex appears as Z1 no later than the final canonicalization pass. Thus the final promoted X0 set and its fixed colors depend only on F.
fixed_conflict_confluence: If an early mandatory singleton conflicts with a later forced assignment or another mandatory singleton, then the same final fixed assignment set contains that conflict.
Hence an early direct UNSAT is not an order artifact; every closure of F is UNSAT.
canonical_partition: Final S_F and final X0_F are order-independent.
Source classes Z2/Z3/Z4 are deterministic functions of the final seed-color masks.
The canonical residual Y0_F is therefore order-independent.
Exact palettes A(v) are deterministic functions of final fixed-color effects from S_F union X0_F and are order-independent.
connectivity_repair_commutation: At any B2B1 repair step, a deleted residual component C is a connected component of G minus the then-current X0 that does not contain the seed.
Therefore C has no nonfixed neighbor outside C at the moment of deletion.
Any later jointly reachable forced vertex lies outside C, so it was already a nonfixed outside vertex at deletion time and is nonadjacent to C.
Any later promoted X0 vertex outside C was likewise nonfixed outside C at deletion time and is nonadjacent to C.
Thus no later jointly reachable operation changes the boundary constraints of an already deleted C.
No future forced assignment may target a vertex of an already deleted C under the joint-reachability guard.
As X0 grows monotonically, removing more fixed vertices can split the retained seed-component but can never reconnect a deleted component.
Consequently sequential repair deletes exactly the vertices outside the seed-connected component of G minus final X0_F, possibly in earlier independent pieces.
List3_terminal_confluence: If a separated component C is UNSAT under its exact P7 List-3 repair instance when deleted, no later jointly reachable force outside C can alter C's lists or boundary.
Therefore batch closure under F contains the same independent UNSAT obstruction.
If C is SAT, its stored coloring obligation remains independent of all later forcing outside C.
reconstruction: Different histories may discover/delete independent repair components at different times and may store different valid List-3 witnesses.
The reconstruction obligation is nevertheless the same factorized relation: color each deleted component from its exact frozen local instance and combine with the final retained-state coloring.

After canonical ordering of deleted vertex sets and deterministic witness selection, receipts can be normalized to the same canonical receipt; without fixing witness selection, they are semantically equivalent up to independent witness choice.
downstream_stack: C0 messages are deterministic functions of final residual components, final fixed-X0 base lists and final dynamic boundaries.
C2 incidences are deterministic functions of the same final remaining graph/component partition.
B2A transition signatures are recomputed from those final C0/C2 objects.
C3 selectors are deterministic functions of final MIN_BAD and D_C data.
Hence the final C0/C2/B2A/C3 architecture is history-order independent.

finite_sanity_receipt.ceiling: Finite sanity supports the algebra only; theorem authority is the structural proof.

consequence.canonical_state_key_can_start_from: compatible forced assignment set F plus deterministic closure, rather than forcing history

explicit_nonclaims: No polynomial bound on the number of compatible forced assignment sets.
No polynomial quotient on assignment sets.
No dependency factorization theorem for B2B2 states.

next_frontier.name: R5_B1B1C5B2B2_B_NEW_SEED_IDENTITY_NECESSITY_AUDIT_V1
next_frontier.target: Determine which future B0/C0/C2/C3/B2A/R1/R2 observables genuinely require identities of newly forced seed vertices beyond aggregate fixed-color effect masks and inherited original provenance.
